title: dcp config get reply (schema MAJOR 1)
description: What Aurora expects from `dcp config get --json --dir <root>`, offered when `dcp version --json` lists the capability `config` with schema_major 1. Unknown fields are ignored; MINOR versions only add optional fields. Exit code 0 with this reply on standard output; any other exit code is a failure and standard error explains it. Every setting the protocol knows is listed, set or not, with its effective value; no setting carries a secret value.

root.description: The repository root the reply is about (absolute path)

revision.description: Opaque token that changes whenever the configuration file changes (for example a hash of its bytes, or `none` when there is no file); `config set --revision` refuses a different one

source.description: The configuration file read (path relative to root, normally .dev-cycle.json), or null when only defaults apply

settings.description: In the order to show them; groups appear in the order of their first setting

findings.description: Configuration problems found (unknown keys, invalid values, legacy keys), never blocking for the reader

value.description: A setting value: boolean, integer, text, list of text, or null when not set (the protocol falls back to detection)

key.description: Dotted path in the configuration file, for example devops.branching or test_commands

group.description: Display group, for example devops, architecture, backlog

description.description: One line on what the setting does

allowed.description: The accepted values of an enum, or of each item of a list; null when any value is accepted

read_only.description: true for mandatory gates and principles, which are shown but cannot be changed

read_only_reason.description: Why it cannot be changed, when read_only is true
